# Private source-write admission experiment

Description before names: each memory miss records one separate decayed request count and returns the prior count under the same history shard mutex. `record_memory_miss` describes that event. Its `memory_miss_counts` map is independent of caller counts and recent trimming events, but shares the caller historian's global atomic request clock and exact `DecayedAccessCount` decay. No conditional-only clock or duplicated decay. Counters live until cache teardown, like caller history, without cap or eviction removal.

At recording, after memory lookup and before disk lookup, read the current global caller request count under the key's history mutex. Return prior decayed conditional demand before adding this request. Carry that f64 across asynchronous disk/source work. Same-key concurrent conditional recordings serialize, so they cannot both observe zero. Other-key caller requests may advance after the snapshot. Memory hits advance the caller clock but never the conditional count. Failed/canceled conditional requests count once if they reached recording. No historian lock is held across cache or I/O calls. Admission never rereads newer demand.

Description before names: `SourceWriteEstimate` represents aligned read/write proxy seconds and expected savings for one offered payload. Read bytes = ceil(max(payload,1)/4096)*4096, requests = ceil(read bytes/1048576). Historical source seconds = 0.108599 + payload * 1.1890459652219313e-8. Historical disk read proxy = requests * 0.00006246274509803923 + aligned bytes * 8.187806372549019e-9. Uncalibrated aligned-payload write proxy reuses that same disk fixed/per-byte formula. It omits metadata, packing loss, checksum, queue/contention, and actual write calibration. No layout changes.

Prior decayed conditional count is explicitly a heuristic for expected future requests reaching disk over a notional future demand horizon comparable to the exponentially weighted past at the caller-request half-life (262144). There is no measured horizon, stationary-demand guarantee, calibrated forecast, or GET-cost claim. Candidate queues only if prior * max(source - disk read proxy,0) > write proxy, strictly. First miss prior zero rejects. Reasons distinguish first miss, no positive savings, insufficient savings, and allowed. Memory insertion and promotion retain baseline code and ordering. Only immediate source enqueue changes. Expanded-range compaction remains unchanged and has zero replay exposure because replay uses whole slices. Covers/redundancy/queue checks can race as before.

Both modes collect conditional demand, source disposition, offered payload/aligned bytes, prior nanocounts and modeled nanoseconds with the same instrumentation. Nanocount/ns counters truncate each observation, not decisions. Source dispositions reconcile successful source callbacks into covered, redundant, expanded, and offered. Offered counts reconcile actual rejection versus enqueue attempts with heuristic reason and payload size band. Distinct queue outcome `policy_savings` joins existing admission balances. Queue/terminal balance is separate from heuristic permission.

Both tier scorers remain fixed256000. Capacities, shard count, pool, history settings, queue, metadata, payload and promotion pipeline remain unchanged. One instrumented binary, baseline mode0 then candidate mode1, one fresh same-host600s pair only.
